newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA PLANS $300 MILLION HOUSE BUILDING TENDER.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA PLANS $300 MILLION HOUSE BUILDING TENDER.

text.p: Romania is to announce a tender next month to build $300 million worth of low-cost housing backed by government guarantees, the ministry of public works said on Monday.

"The tender papers are ready and the bid will open in April, as soon as the 1997 state budget clears parliament," the ministry's Secretary of State, Laszlo Borbely, told Reuters. "The deadline for the bidders will be in June."

He said the sums to pay back successful bidders -- expected to be construction and investment companies -- would come from the state budget, local budgets where houses are erected and from prospective house buyers.
Under the draft 1997 budget now before parliament, the government has allocated 373 billion lei ($53.3 million) for house rehabilitation and building.
Borbely said that was insufficient to meet demand for relatively low-cost homes, but could not specify how many units would be built within the $300 million project.
"We hope we will be able to open these homes by the end of 1998," he said.
Romania faces a housing shortage, with 500,000 applications for state housing unmet, mainly from young couples hit by plunging living standards since the 1989 fall of communism.
